findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size rewritten with incompatible Java MessageFormat syntax, breaking i18next interpolation
findings.body: The key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This file is consumed by the Account Console React app via i18next, which uses double-curly-brace interpolation (`{{0}}`), as confirmed by every other key in the same file (e.g. `backTo=Back to {{app}}`, `setUpNew=Set up {{name}}`). Switching to single braces means `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` will no longer be substituted by i18next, and the Java `MessageFormat` ChoiceFormat fragment `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is not valid i18next syntax at all, so it will be rendered verbatim to end users instead of the pluralized word. This is a functional regression in the Account Console error message, seemingly caused by blindly applying the Java-properties fix for this key to the JS i18next resource file as well.

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size rewritten with incompatible Java MessageFormat syntax in Admin Console i18next resources
findings.body: Same issue as in the account-ui file: `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` was changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The surrounding keys in this file use i18next double-brace interpolation, so this change breaks placeholder substitution and introduces a literal, unparsed ChoiceFormat string that will be shown to admins instead of a correctly pluralized message when editing multivalued user/client attributes.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The key `totpStep1` was changed from the (stale, link-containing) Lithuanian text to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This is a user-visible content defect: Lithuanian users configuring an authenticator will now see an unrelated Italian sentence instead of a Lithuanian translation. This appears to be a copy/paste mistake made while fixing the illegal anchor tags flagged by the new sanitizer.

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The key `loginTotpStep1` was changed from the Lithuanian text (which previously contained mismatched FreeOTP/Google Play anchor tags) to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian rather than Lithuanian. This is the same mistake as in the account messages file for the same locale and key, and results in Lithuanian users seeing Italian text on the login TOTP setup page.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) file now uses Traditional Chinese phrasing
findings.body: The key `totpStep1` was changed to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters/terminology (手機, 裝, 應用程式) rather than Simplified Chinese (which would use 手机, 装, 应用). Since this file is the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) locale resource, this introduces a script/locale inconsistency that should instead read with Simplified characters, e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：

findings.title: Property files are read with default ISO-8859-1 decoding although they contain raw UTF-8 text
findings.body: `bundle = new PropertyResourceBundle(fis)` (and the equivalent call for the English counterpart) uses the InputStream-based constructor, which per the Properties/PropertyResourceBundle contract decodes content as ISO-8859-1. The actual theme message files (as shown throughout this PR, e.g. Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Greek text) are UTF-8 encoded with literal multi-byte characters, not `\uXXXX`-escaped ASCII. Reading them through the InputStream constructor will corrupt all non-ASCII text used for comparisons and for the diff snippets emitted in error messages, making the tool's diagnostic output unreliable/garbled for the vast majority of real locale files. The code should decode explicitly as UTF-8 (e.g. via `InputStreamReader`/`PropertyResourceBundle(Reader)`).

findings.title: Fragile string-substitution derivation of the English source file path
findings.body: The path to the English counterpart file is computed with `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This blindly rewrites any occurrence of the literal substring "resources-community" anywhere in the absolute path, and assumes the file name's final underscore-delimited segment is exactly the locale suffix. This is fragile: a checkout path containing "resources-community" elsewhere would be mis-rewritten, and file names containing an underscore before the locale code in a different position (e.g. a base name with an embedded underscore) will compute a non-existent English file name. In fact, the accompanying test had to rename `duplicate_keys.properties` to `duplicateKeys_en.properties` specifically to avoid the mid-name underscore being matched by this regex and resolving to a nonexistent `duplicate_en.properties`, which demonstrates the fragility of this approach in production use.

findings.title: Unchecked RuntimeException thrown instead of using the MojoExecutionException error-reporting path
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml()` wraps IOExceptions (e.g. missing/English file not found) in `RuntimeException` rather than propagating through the `MojoExecutionException` used by `verify()`/`verifyNoDuplicateKeys`. Since `verify()`'s try/catch only catches `IOException`, any IO failure inside `verifySafeHtml()` surfaces as an unchecked `RuntimeException` with a raw stack trace rather than being reported through the structured `messages` list or wrapped the same way other failures are, producing an inconsistent and less actionable failure mode for the Maven build.

findings.title: Choice-format normalization is hardcoded to specific key names, which will miss future keys using the same syntax
findings.body: `normalizeValue` only strips MessageFormat ChoiceFormat syntax (which legitimately contains `<`) for keys matching `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit`, or exactly `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. Any new or existing message key elsewhere in the codebase that uses `{n,choice,...}` syntax with a `<` character (a common pattern for pluralization) but isn't in this hardcoded list will be incorrectly flagged as illegal HTML by this verifier, producing false positives that block legitimate translations/content unless the hardcoded list is remembered and updated every time such a key is added.

findings.title: Anchor-tag validation assumes identical ordering between translation and English source
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` walks through anchor tags in the translated value and the English value in lockstep using two independent `Matcher.find()` calls, requiring the Nth anchor tag in the translation to exactly equal the Nth anchor tag in English. Legitimate translations frequently reorder embedded markup (e.g. due to different sentence/grammar structure, as is common for RTL or SOV languages), which would cause a correct translation with the same set of anchors (just reordered) to be reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string", a false positive that would block otherwise-valid translations from passing verification.

findings.title: No test coverage for non-ASCII/UTF-8 property content
findings.body: All added test fixtures (`illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_en.properties`, `noHtml_de.properties`, `changedAnchor_en.properties`, `changedAnchor_de.properties`) use plain ASCII content. None of the tests exercise a file containing multi-byte UTF-8 characters (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, etc.), even though essentially all real translated message files in this repository contain such content and the tool reads files via an InputStream-based `PropertyResourceBundle` that decodes as ISO-8859-1. This gap means the encoding-corruption problem for non-ASCII translations is not caught by the test suite.
